# 2 Samuel Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 186v–187r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_016_page_001.jpg, 2SA_016_page_002.jpg

---

**16:1** And-David passed a-little from the-summit, and-behold, Tsiva servant of-Mefiboshet [came]-to-meet-him, and-a-pair of-donkeys saddled, and-upon-them two-hundred [loaves of]-bread and-a-hundred [cakes of]-raisins and-a-hundred [cakes of]-summer-fruit [qayits] and-a-skin [nevel] of-wine.

**16:2** And-said the-king to Tsiva, "What [are]-these to-you?" And-said Tsiva, "The-donkeys [are] for-[the]-house of-the-king to-ride, and-the-bread and-the-summer-fruit [are] for-the-young-men to-eat, and-the-wine [is] for-the-faint [yya'ef] in-the-wilderness to-drink."

**16:3** And-said the-king, "And-where [is the]-son of-your-master?" And-said Tsiva to the-king, "Behold, [he-is]-sitting in-Yerushalayim, for he-said, 'Today will-restore to-me [the]-house of-Yisra'el [the]-kingdom [mamlakhut] of-my-father.'"

**16:4** And-said the-king to Tsiva, "Behold, to-you [is] all that [belongs]-to-Mefiboshet." And-said Tsiva, "I-bow-down [hishtachaveti]. Let-me-find favor [chen] in-your-eyes, my-lord the-king."

**16:5** And-came the-king David to Bachurim, and-behold, from-there [was]-coming-out a-man from-[the]-clan [mishpachat] of-[the]-house of-Sha'ul, and-his-name [was] Shim'i son of-Gera, coming-out, coming-out and-cursing [meqallel].

**16:6** And-he-threw [vayesaqqel] stones at-David and-at all [the]-servants of-the-king David, and-all the-people and-all the-mighty-men [gibborim] [were] at-his-right and-at-his-left.

**16:7** And-thus said Shim'i in-his-cursing, "Go-out, go-out [tse, tse], man of-blood [ish ha-damim] and-man of-the-worthless [ish ha-beliyya'al]!

**16:8** Returned upon-you YHWH all [the]-blood of-[the]-house of-Sha'ul, in-whose-place you-reigned, and-gave YHWH the-kingdom into-[the]-hand of-Avshalom your-son. And-behold-you in-your-evil [ra'ah], for a-man of-blood [ish damim] [are]-you!"

**16:9** And-said Avishai son of-Tseruyah to the-king, "Why should-curse this dead dog [ha-kelev ha-met ha-zeh] my-lord the-king? Let-me-cross-over, please, and-I-will-remove his-head."

**16:10** And-said the-king, "What [is]-to-me and-to-you [mah-li ve-lakhem], sons of-Tseruyah? For-he-curses, and-for YHWH said to-him, 'Curse David' — and-who will-say, 'Why did-you-do thus?'"

**16:11** And-said David to Avishai and-to all his-servants, "Behold, my-son, who came-out from-my-inward-parts [mimme'ai], seeks my-life [nafshi]. And-how-much-more now [the]-son of-[the]-Binyamini? Leave-him [hannichhu-lo], and-let-him-curse, for YHWH said to-him.

**16:12** Perhaps YHWH will-see with-his-eye [be'eyniy — Qere: be-'on'yi, 'in my affliction'], and-return YHWH to-me good [tovah] in-place-of [tachat] his-cursing this day."

**16:13** And-went David and-his-men on-the-road, and-Shim'i [was]-going on [the]-rib [tsela'] of-the-mountain opposite-him, going and-cursing, and-threw stones opposite-him and-threw-dust [ve'iffer be'afar].

**16:14** And-came the-king and-all the-people that [were]-with-him weary ['ayefim], and-he-refreshed-himself [vayyinnafesh] there.

**16:15** And-Avshalom and-all the-people, [the]-men of-Yisra'el, came to-Yerushalayim, and-Achitofel [was]-with-him.

**16:16** And-it-was when-came Chushai the-Arki, friend [re'eh] of-David, to Avshalom, and-said Chushai to Avshalom, "Long-live [yechi] the-king! Long-live the-king!"

**16:17** And-said Avshalom to Chushai, "This [is]-your-covenant-faithfulness [chesed] with your-friend [re'ekha]? Why did-you-not go with your-friend?"

**16:18** And-said Chushai to Avshalom, "No, for whom YHWH has-chosen and-this people and-all [the]-men of-Yisra'el — to-him I-will-be, and-with-him I-will-dwell.

**16:19** And-the-second-[thing]: whom shall-I serve? [Is-it]-not before his-son? As I-served before your-father, so I-will-be before-you."

**16:20** And-said Avshalom to Achitofel, "Give to-you counsel [etsah]: what shall-we-do?"

**16:21** And-said Achitofel to Avshalom, "Go to [the]-concubines of-your-father that he-left to-keep the-house, and-will-hear all Yisra'el that you-have-made-yourself-odious [niv'ashta] with your-father, and-will-be-strengthened [the]-hands of-all who [are]-with-you."

**16:22** And-they-pitched [vayattu] for-Avshalom the-tent upon the-roof, and-went-in Avshalom to [the]-concubines of-his-father before-[the]-eyes of-all Yisra'el.

**16:23** And-[the]-counsel of-Achitofel that he-counseled in-those days [was] as-that-which one-inquires [yish'al] of-[the]-word of-God. Thus [was] all [the]-counsel of-Achitofel, both to-David and-also to-Avshalom.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — Tsiva/Ziba:** Ziba is the servant assigned to Mephibosheth's household (2 Sam 9:2-10). His arrival with provisions appears generous, but his report about Mephibosheth in v.3 is self-serving. The narrator leaves the truth unresolved until 19:24-30, where Mephibosheth gives a contradictory account.

**v.5 — meqallel, coming out and cursing:** The infinitive absolute construction *yatso yatso u-meqallel* intensifies the action — Shimei comes out *relentlessly* cursing. The participle *meqallel* (cursing) indicates continuous action.

**v.7 — ish ha-damim ve-ish ha-beliyya'al:** "Man of blood and man of worthlessness" — the double epithet is a comprehensive curse. *Ish damim* accuses David of bloodshed (perhaps the blood of Saul's house); *beliyya'al* is a term of utter contempt, later associated with demonic opposition.

**v.10 — mah-li ve-lakhem:** "What to me and to you?" — a formula of disassociation (cf. 2 Kgs 3:13; John 2:4). David refuses to identify with the sons of Zeruiah's instinct for violence. This formula occurs at key moments when David restrains those who would act violently on his behalf.

**v.12 — Ketiv/Qere:** The Leningrad Codex preserves a significant Ketiv/Qere variant. The Ketiv (written text) reads *be'eyniy* ("with his eye/in his seeing"), while the Qere (reading tradition) reads *be'on'yi* ("in my affliction"). The Qere makes better sense: David hopes YHWH will see his affliction and repay good for the cursing.

**v.21 — niv'ashta:** The hithpael of *ba'ash* — "you have made yourself stink/become odious." Ahithophel's counsel is that by publicly violating David's concubines, Absalom will make reconciliation with David impossible, thereby strengthening the resolve of his followers. The act fulfills Nathan's prophecy in 12:11-12.

**v.22 — upon the roof:** The tent is pitched on the palace roof — the same roof from which David saw Bathsheba (11:2). The location is not accidental. Nathan prophesied "you did it in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun" (12:12). The roof is the site of the curse coming full circle.

**v.23 — counsel like the word of God:** The narrator's comment elevates Ahithophel's counsel to near-prophetic status. This observation serves the narrative tension: if Ahithophel's counsel is as reliable as a divine oracle, then only divine intervention can overthrow it (cf. 17:14).

*— EMET*
